# Q06 quest handlers (crafting, ascension): deviations and generated files

## P6-Q asc-hand (2026-09-29): the four retail ascension quests

The first hand-ported quest handlers of phase 6 (owner, 2026-09-29 00:35: "Try to prioritize things that would get Ascension running
sooner"; U1/U7: in their own chunk, in a spare build slot, reverted rather than fixed forward if a phase-5 gate turns red). questgen refuses
all four files (`python -m tools.gen.questgen --only ascension/...`: `CustomConfig.ENABLE_SIMPLE_2NDCLASS` in each, two lambdas and
`ClassChangeService.setClass` in 1006, two lambdas and `new SM_ASCENSION_MORPH` in 2008), so they are ported by hand, statement by statement,
in the conventions of questgen's output for their sibling `_1913DispatchtoVerteron` (the prelude, `runtime::Ptr` locals, `runtime::as` /
`runtime::cast` for `instanceof` and casts, `static_cast<int8_t>` headings, `::aion::gameserver::world::getId(WorldMapType::X)`,
`::aion::gameserver::model::getStartingClass`, `AION_QUEST_HANDLER` at the end).

| C++ (handlers/aion/gameserver/handlers/quest/ascension/) | Java (game-server/data/handlers/quest/ascension/) |
|---|---|
| `_1006Ascension.cpp` | `_1006Ascension.java` |
| `_2008Ascension.cpp` | `_2008Ascension.java` |
| `_1007ACeremonyinSanctum.cpp` | `_1007ACeremonyinSanctum.java` |
| `_2009ACeremonyinPandaemonium.cpp` | `_2009ACeremonyinPandaemonium.java` |

The twelve dispatch quests of the directory (1913-1916, 19070/19071, 2901-2904, 29070/29071) are the route-gen lane's (questgen output).

### Shapes that are not behaviour changes

| Area | Java | C++ | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| The raiders' task (`_1006Ascension.java:164-175`, `_2008Ascension.java:226-237`) | `ThreadPoolManager.getInstance().schedule(() -> {...}, 43000)` capturing `qs`, `env` and `player` | `ThreadPoolManager::getInstance().schedule({this, &pinnedPlayer, &env, &pinnedQs}, [..] {...}, 43000)`: the pinned form of the runtime (ThreadPoolManager.h), the idiom `AbstractQuestHandler::useQuestItem` uses for its own 3-second task; the handler is Immortal (RT-11) | The runtime's scheduling rule (design §7.1, lint L5): a task pins the RefCounted objects it captures by reference |
| `case SETPRO3:` (1006), `case SETPRO4:` (1006), `case SETPRO6:` (2008) | A local declared in a `case` of the switch | The case body in braces | C++ forbids jumping past an initialization; the local is read in its own case only |
| `Npc` list of the raiders | `List<Npc> mobs = new ArrayList<>()` | `std::vector<runtime::Ptr<Npc>>` | Local container (the rule QuestItemNpcAI.cpp follows) |
| `if (CustomConfig.ENABLE_SIMPLE_2NDCLASS) return;` in `register()` | A static boolean | The `std::atomic<bool>` read through its implicit conversion (a sequentially consistent load, as `PlayerController.cpp:700` reads `ENABLE_STARTER_KIT`) | Not `.load()`: tools/parity counts that as a call Java does not make (review of 2026-09-29) |
| `setPlayerClass(env, qs, playerClass)` | `qs` is unused | Unused as well (the parameter is kept) | Faithful signature |

### tools/parity

`python tools/parity/parity.py pair <java> <cpp>` over the four files: `_1007ACeremonyinSanctum` and `_2009ACeremonyinPandaemonium` are at
parity (0 mismatches). `_1006Ascension` and `_2008Ascension` differ in calls-multiset and calls-order only, in the raiders' list: Java's
`new ArrayList<>()` and four `add` against four `push_back` of the local `std::vector` (literals, operators, constants, spawn ids and the
spawn analyzer are at parity). phase6-inventory.md §7.6 item 1 wants parity green before merge, and tools/parity has neither a rename for
this idiom nor the `// parity:` waiver yet (its README: not implemented). The tool is the route-gen / P6-T lane's, so this lane did not edit
it. **Integrator decision needed** for the two files: a rename rule in tools/parity (`push_back` -> `add`, a declared local `std::vector`
for `new ArrayList`), a waiver, or the list spelled as the runtime's `runtime::ArrayList` shim (a monitor-guarded list for a four-element
local, against the runtime's rule for locals).

**Integration decision (2026-09-29, `p6q/ascension-route`):** the rename rule. tools/parity now documents C++ `push_back` as `add` (the
java.util.List-on-std::vector renames `front`/`back`/`empty` already had) and a Java `new ArrayList<>()` without an argument as no call (the
default-constructed local); with an argument it stays a call. **All four files are at parity**, and questgen's 929 emitted files stay at
parity (docs/design/p6q-ascension-route.md).

### Java behaviour kept (`// java-bug kept` in the code)

| Where | Java behaviour | Effect on the route |
|---|---|---|
| The raiders' task | Not cancelled when he dies or leaves within the 43 s: `onDieEvent` sets the var back to 3 / 4, then the task sets 51 and spawns the four raiders at the arena's coordinates of whatever map instance he is in | A death during the flight leaves him at var 51 with raiders in his bind map; not reached on the normal route |
| `SETPRO1` of 1006 and 2008 | No var guard: the action sets var 1 and beams him again at any START var | A client that sends it late restarts the mission (the client offers the action at var 0 only) |
| `SETPRO3` of 1006 (`_1006Ascension.java:97-103`) | No var guard: at any START var the action opens a new Karamatis B instance, beams him in, sets var 99 and takes Daminu's Essence | The client offers the action on page 1693 only, at var 3 |

**Retail design, not a bug (the owner, 2026-09-29; owner-decisions.md, "2026-09-29 (answers)")**: `onQuestCompletedEvent` of 1006 / 2008
with `QuestService.finishQuest` (QuestService.java:103-113). `finishQuest` gives the reward's exp (quest_data.xml:66 and :9300,
`exp="73200"`) **before** it sets COMPLETE and fires `onQuestCompleted`, whose `updateDaeva()` makes him a Daeva; `PlayerCommonData.setExp`
holds a starting class or a non-Daeva at level 9 with the full bar (exp 126,069). This was recorded here as a kept Java bug ("the 73,200 exp
are lost"); the owner answered that it is how the retail chain worked: "the Ascension quest would basically put you at maximum EXP at level 9,
and then the next quest would bump you over". The new Gladiator stays level 9 with a full bar until his next exp: the ceremony's 13,125 exp
(1007 / 2009), a kill, or a relog (the offline `setExp` finds 1006 / 2008 COMPLETE and lets him be level 10). The two handlers carry a
comment saying so in place of the `// java-bug kept` marker, and the same cases pin it:
`Quest1006Test.TheRewardBeamsHimToPoetaFinishesTheQuestMakesADaevaAndStarts1007`, `AQuesterBelowAFullBarReachesTheCapWithTheRewardExp`,
`Quest2008Test.TheRewardInAtaxiarBeamsHimToIshalgenMakesADaevaAndStarts2009` and gs.scenario.ascension E5 (SM_STATUPDATE_EXP: 43,087 of 43,087, the full level-9 bar); the ceremony's exp lifts him
(`CeremonyTest.JucleasGivesAWarriorVarTenAndRewardGroupZeroAndMacusFinishesWithLevelTen`, and E6: 13,125 above level 10's first exp, before
any relog). No test name said "bug", so none was renamed.

Also as Java, and not marked: `onItemUseEvent` of 1006 answers `HandlerResult.SUCCESS` outside the item-use zone (`// ??` in Java);
`onKillEvent` of 1006 answers false for Orissan (QuestEngine.onKill ignores the answer); `SELECT5_1` of 2008 answers false after its movie,
so CM_DIALOG_SELECT goes on to the npc's own dialog; `onDieEvent` of 1006 sets var 5 back to 3 although `onEnterWorldEvent` keeps 5 (dying
at var 5 is not reachable: every npc of the instance is deleted with Orissan).

### Engine pieces on the route

No engine body was ported: everything the four handlers call was ported by M5d, M5e C-01 and the M5f instance core. Two engine sites are
reached on the route and stay as they are (reported, not changed; they belong to other chunks):

| Site | What the route sees |
|---|---|
| `AbyssPointsService::addAp(Player&, VisibleObject&, int)` (`services/abyss/AbyssPointsService.cpp:31`, `AION_UNPORTED`, P5-12b) | Reached by `NpcController::doReward` for each raider and for Orissan / Hellion (AscensationNpcAI answers REWARD_AP): 5 kills per race. It throws after `QuestEngine.onKill`, the exp and the DP, so the quest counts every kill and the handler has already deleted the npc. The throw unwinds to the try of `NpcController.onDie` (NpcController.cpp:176-185, NpcController.java:147-156) and skips there: the AP itself, `DropRegistrationService.registerDrop` for the winner (the rest of `doReward`), `instanceHandler.onDie(npc)` and `ai.onGeneralEvent(DIED)` (DiedEventHandler). Low impact here: Karamatis B and Ataxiar B have no instance handler of their own, and the handler deleted the npc already. The game server logs `onDie() exception` per kill. Not ported by this lane: the Java body calls the unported `SiegeService.onAbyssPointsAdded`, and the phase-5 test `AttackSeamTest.DoRewardReachesTheRealPvEApGainedBeforeTheUnportedAbyssPointsService` pins the throw, so a port here would turn a phase-5 test red (U7). m5d-plan.md §18.8 item 6's premise ("no start map spawns such an npc") no longer holds once these handlers register. **Integrator / owner decision needed**: port it with P5-12b, or accept the skipped AP and the log line per kill until then |
| `WebRewardService::MaxLevelReward::reward` (`AION_UNPORTED`) | Called by `onQuestCompletedEvent` only while `isPendingAscension`, which nothing in the port sets: not reached |

### Files outside the chunk

No header changed, so no header request. `tests/scenario/AscensionScenarioTest.cpp` and the `gs.scenario.ascension` registration in
`tests/scenario/ScenarioTests.cmake` (and its runtime in the file's slot table) are P5-SC's directory: the lane held a lease of it
(`aion_gs_chunk(Q06 LEASE PHASE 6 TEST_SUPPORT scenario)`), which the integration released (the file is handed to P5-SC; the lease row
turned the phase-5 test `tools.porting` red, docs/design/p6q-ascension-route.md), and chunks.cmake gives Q06 the new test directory `tests/quest_handlers_ascension`
(`TESTS quest_handlers_ascension`). The unit fixture includes tests/instance's `AscensionTestSupport.h` / `AscensionTestData.h` by relative
path, unchanged (its instance npc rows keep their `<equipment>`, so the unit run logs `NpcEquipmentList.items` NullPointerExceptions from
SM_NPC_INFO when the quester meets them: noise, no case reads it).

### Mutation proof (AION_ASC_MUT)

The lane's first proof (18 mutants M1-M18) failed 20 of its 51 cases; the review (2026-09-29) found 14 non-equivalent mutants that no unit
case failed (R4, R5, T3 and U2 passed the scenario too), and asked for a mutant per case. The review fixes added the cases above and redid
the proof: 73 mutant schemata in the four handler files behind `AION_ASC_MUT=<id>[,<id>...]` (a class-static switch per class: the registry
scan forbids a namespace-scope `static` in handler files), after saving the files and their sha256. The unit executable was rebuilt and run
once per id:
the unmutated run passes 67/67, **every one of the 67 cases fails on at least one mutant**, and every mutant fails at least one case except
D6, which only the scenario can see. The ids re-express the lane's M1-M18 (named in the table) and the review's survivors R1, R4, R5, R6,
S1-S4, T1-T4, U1, U2. C12 survived the first round: `PernosOpens1011AtVarZeroAnd1013AtVarOne` expected SETPRO1 at var 2 to answer false,
and the mutant's beam into the missing Sanctum answered false as well (through QuestEngine.onDialog's catch); the case now checks that the
var stays 2 and that he is not despawned, and the second and third rounds (the third with the class-static switch that the game server
build needs) fail it.

passed).

The sources were then restored from the saved copies, their sha256 verified equal to the saved ones (1006 `7a936aca...`, 2008

in P5-05.md and P5-09a.md are earlier lanes' uses of the same name).

## Generated dispatches

P6-Q ascension route, lane route-gen (2026-09-29). The 12 dispatch quests of `game-server/data/handlers/quest/ascension/` are generated by
`cpp/tools/gen/questgen` into `game-server/handlers/aion/gameserver/handlers/quest/ascension/` and compiled into `aion_gs_handlers_quest_q06`.
The generator change, the golden trace harness (Q05's test directory), the mutation proof and the gate impact are described once, in
[Q05.md](Q05.md). The hand ports of this directory (1006, 2008, 1007, 2009) are another
lane's and are described in their own sections of this file.

### Generated files

Tier A, one statement tree each (register: `registerOnQuestCompleted` and two talk npcs; a two-step talk chain; `defaultOnQuestCompletedEvent`):
`_1913DispatchtoVerteron`, `_1914DispatchtoVerteron`, `_1915DispatchtoVerteron`, `_1916DispatchtoVerteron`, `_19070ADispatchtoVerteron`,
`_19071ADispatchtoVerteron` (Elyos, after 1007 by reward group: quest_data.xml `start_conditions`), `_2901DispatchtoAltgard`,
`_2902DispatchtoAltgard`, `_2903DispatchtoAltgard`, `_2904DispatchtoAltgard`, `_29070ADispatchtoAltgard`, `_29071ADispatchtoAltgard`
(Asmodian, after 2009).

**No hand edit**: `tools/gen/tests/test_questgen_tree.py` regenerates each file and compares the bytes. Regenerate (from `cpp/`):
`python -m tools.gen.questgen --dry-run --emit <dir outside the repo> --only ascension/<file>.java ...` and copy the `.cpp` files. None of
the 12 reads `CustomConfig.ENABLE_SIMPLE_2NDCLASS`; they register in every gate profile. Nothing starts them before 1007 / 2009 complete, so
they are inert in the phase-5 gates (m5a, m5b, m5b2 measured green with them in).

### Tests

The oracle's route slice (`tools/oracle/questtrace/extract.py` `SLICE_ROUTE`) traces the 12 whole: 17 cases each, 204 in all, in
`tools/oracle/expected/quest/<id>.json`; `tests/test_quest_trace.py` `RouteSliceTest` checks 1913's registration and cases against values
derived by hand from `_1913DispatchtoVerteron.java`. Q05's golden harness compiles the 12 files by `#include`
(`tests/quest_handlers_golden/GoldenAscensionHandlers.cpp`) and runs every case through the real engine: **204 of 204 pass** (708
compared runs with the overlays of Q05.md), and their registration traces match. The chain trigger is checked: the overlay with 1007 / 2009
finished at the reward group the start condition names, a class the quest permits and its level starts the dispatch (and one level below
does nothing), so a dispatch whose `onQuestCompletedEvent` does not call `defaultOnQuestCompletedEvent` fails (mutant `q1913_done`), as do an
end npc that rewards at any npc (`q29071_endnpc`), `var + 2` and START for REWARD.

### Deviations

None. Java's behaviour is kept statement by statement.
